A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of conditionally patho - genic mycobacteria (MAH) in the environment of one herd of breeding swine, as a result of the use of contaminated feedstuffs, was a major reason for the high number of animals with dubious responses to tuberculin skin tests with avian tuberculins.
the most effective method for the diagnosis of avian TB is the post mortem examination, and for prevention of its spread, the use of disinfection and vaccination.
the most effective method for the control of avian tuberculosis in pigs is the elimination of the source of infection, i.e. the birds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of CPM in the environment of a pig farm may be a cause of non-specific reactions in tuberculin tests.

the presence of CPM in the environment can lead to false positive results of tuberculin skin tests in pigs and that the implementation of appropriate hygiene measures can reduce the risk of false positive results.

it is possible to reduce the number of animals with positive responses to avi- an tuberculin, and to reduce the risk of infection of the herd by avian tuberculosis, by taking preventive measures against the presence of CPM in the environment.
